checks.sourceSays: "Step 6 : IF forwards recommendations to Deputy Chief Inspector of Factories (DCIF) for allotment of Registration Number within 12 days of submission of correct and complete application. Step 7 : DCIF sends recommendation to Chief Inspector of Factories (CIF) within 8 days of receipt of recommendation from IF. Step 8 : Allotment of Registration number and issuance of licence with intimation to the concerned DCIF / IF within 10 days from the receipt of recommendation from DCIF." The three notified sub-limits total exactly 30 days, confirming the ED's 30-day figure and its 12-day first leg. The same document also resolves the ED's own VAGUE gap about deficiency cycles: "In case of any clarifications, the applicant is informed on actions to be taken and start date will be after all the clarifications have been received."

checks.sourceSays: The Jharkhand Gazette (Extraordinary) No. 165 of 9th April 2025 notifies the Jharkhand Factories (Amendment) Rules, 2025: "Substitution of Schedule- A, B & C under Sub rule (1) of Rule (5) of the Jharkhand Factories Rules, 1950 'Schedule- 'A' 'B' and ' C' of the said Rules shall be Substituted by new Schedule 'A' 'B' and ' C' which are annexed here to.'" The annexed Schedule-'A' (Rule-5), 'Scale of fees payable for Grant of licence and Annual fees for Factories defined under section 2 (m) of the Factories Act, 1948 Other than Electricity Generating, Transforming Factories', is a complete 12-row x 12-column matrix. It confirms the ED's two sample rows exactly (Nil HP: 530 / 2,060 / 2,380; Not Exceeding 10 HP: 1,190 / 2,110 / 2,900) and supplies every figure the ED record omitted, e.g. Not Exceeding 50 HP: 2,380 / 3,430 / 3,960 / 5,540 / 8,710 / 11,350 / 16,370 / 18,480 / 26,400 / 52,800 / 63,360 / 1,58,400; Not Exceeding 500 HP: 28,510 / 35,640 / 37,620 / 39,600 / 43,560 / 55,680 / 65,660 / 74,250 / 1,33,650 / 1,67,150 / 2,60,490 / 3,86,100; and Above 25,000 HP: 1,11,470 / 2,04,140 / 2,41,560 / 3,24,720 / 3,61,550 / 4,00,360 / 4,35,600 / 5,18,760 / 6,33,600 / 6,69,240 / 6,73,200 / 7,12,800 across the 20 / 50 / 100 / 250 / 500 / 750 / 1,000 / 2,000 / 5,000 / 10,000 / 25,000 / Over-25,000 worker columns. Schedule-'B' gives the KW-based scale for electricity generating and transforming stations (Not exceeding 50 KW: Rs 990 generating / Rs 590 transforming, rising to Above 7,00,000 KW: Rs 2,21,760 / Rs 1,42,560) and adds "b) All transmitting stations (Factories) Rs. 22,500.00". Schedule-'C' sets "Rs. 1000" for factories declared under Section 85. The same notification confirms the ED's amendment fee: "The fee for the amendment of License shall be one thousand rupees.", and adds a figure the ED did not carry: "The fee for transfer of License shall be one thousand rupees and shall be payable by the new Occupier applying for transfer of License under sub rule (1)."

The companion SOP adds "Copy of Project Report", "ID proof of Land / Building Owner", "Address Proof of Land / Building Owner", and lists among the online Form II fields "Brief of manufacturing process", "Total Power installed", "Generator capacity", "Transformer capacity" and "Map approval letter number and date". The form itself is confirmed as "FORM No. 2 — Application for Registration and grant or Renewal of license for the year ....and Notice of occupation specified in, Sections 6 and 7 to be submitted in triplicate." Every ED line item is matched; the only ED item with no direct counterpart in the official checklist is 'Approved building or site plan documents', which appears instead as the Form II field 'Map approval letter number and date'.

remarks: TRANSPORT NOTE — how the previously-blocked state portal was unlocked, and why no http fallback was needed. shramadhan.jharkhand.gov.in and jiada.jharkhand.gov.in were excluded in the earlier pass for 'SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate'. The cause was diagnosed this session: the server presents ONLY its leaf certificate (C=IN, ST=Jharkhand, L=Ranchi, O=Jharkhand agency for promotion of information technology, CN=*.jharkhand.gov.in, valid 28 Jul 2026 - 7 Feb 2027) and omits the intermediate. The missing intermediate was downloaded from the address published in the leaf's own Authority Information Access extension (http://secure.globalsign.com/cacert/gsgccr46ovtlsca2025.crt = 'GlobalSign GCC R46 OV TLS CA 2025'), and that intermediate was independently verified to chain to 'GlobalSign Root R46' already present in the session CA bundle (openssl verify -CAfile /root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt returned OK, and the leaf then verified OK with the intermediate supplied as untrusted). Every fetch above therefore ran over fully-verified TLS with the chain completed, NOT over http and NOT with verification disabled, so every citation is marked transport 'https'. http:// was tried first on shramadhan and simply timed out, so the Kerala-style http fallback would not have worked here.

DEEMED APPROVAL — why the verdict is not_found rather than confirmed or contradicted, and the unresolved tension a reviewer should see. No document on the Labour Department's own Factories Act shelf states either that deemed approval exists for the Factory Licence or that it does not; the official SOP simply ends at Step 8 (issuance) with no consequence attached to the 30-day limit lapsing, so the ED's 'no' is unrebutted but also unconfirmed. Against that, two independently-verified official sources show deemed approval IS part of the framework this licence sits inside. (a) The Department of Industries page on the state portal says of the Jharkhand Industries Facilitation and Single Window Clearance Bill: 'It is a landmark bill for the investors as it includes provisions such as Deemed Approval, Self-certification, Third party inspections and Appeals among others' (https://jharkhand.gov.in/industries). (b) The gazette-published Jharkhand Industrial and Investment Policy 2021 lists 'Grant and renewal of Factory License' among the services delivered through that single-window system, and provides that the State Grievance Redressal Committee 'shall discuss the numbers as well as the reasons of the Deemed Approvals proposed by the concerned department and also suggest the department to provide the approvals on time in the future' - language that presumes deemed approvals are actually being issued somewhere in the single-window estate. Neither source names the Factory Licence as a notified deemed-approval clearance, and no notification listing the deemed-approval services could be reached this session, so the specific ED claim could not be confirmed or contradicted. A reviewer should treat 'Jharkhand has no deemed approval for Factory Licence' as the issuing officer's statement about his own service rather than as a settled statement about state law.

AUTOMATIC ISSUANCE ALREADY EXISTS FOR RENEWALS - a materially different fact from the ED record, and arguably the strongest counterweight to the ED's deemed-approval reform recommendation. An order of the Chief Inspector of Factories, Jharkhand (Order No. EODB/CIF/2020-120, Ranchi, dated 02/12/2020, read from the scanned Hindi original by page render) provides that under Section 6 of the Factories Act 1948 and Rule 07 of the Jharkhand Factories Rules 1950, factory licence renewal is applied for online at https://advantage.jharkhand.gov.in/SingleWindow under the 'AUTO RENEWAL' option with no additional documents or papers required, and that on the basis of previously-held data the licence is issued online as 'AUTO RENEWED' in a 'TRANSPARENT', 'AUTO' and 'NON DISCRETIONARY' manner once the applicant pays the prescribed fee online; the order records that this arrangement took effect in the state from 01-11-2020. This is non-discretionary automatic issuance for the RENEWAL of a Factory Licence, which the ED record does not mention at all. It does not contradict the ED's deemedApproval entry, which is scoped to fresh grant after the 30-day window, but it does mean the ED's reform proposal ('introduce statutory deemed approval for complete, low-risk applications') would be extending to first-time grant a mechanism the state already operates for renewal. The Industrial and Investment Policy 2021 corroborates the renewal simplification independently: licence under the Factories Act, 1948 is one of 7 services where 'Businesses can now get the renewals by paying the required fees without the need for filling the forms and uploading the documents again.'

TIMELINE - the 30 days is a sum of three notified legs, not a single notified figure, and the clock-restart rule resolves an ED gap. The ED reported '30 days overall with a 12-day sub-deadline'; the official SOP shows the full decomposition as 12 days (Inspector of Factories to Deputy Chief Inspector) + 8 days (DCIF to Chief Inspector) + 10 days (CIF allotment and issuance) = 30. No source states a single consolidated 30-day statutory SLA, so the ED's figure is correct as an arithmetic total of the notified legs. Separately, the ED record carried a VAGUE gap asking what happens to the 30-day window when deficiency/resubmission cycles intervene; the official document answers it directly - 'In case of any clarifications, the applicant is informed on actions to be taken and start date will be after all the clarifications have been received' - i.e. the clock restarts from the date the last clarification is received, and the 12-day leg runs only from 'submission of correct and complete application'. Elapsed calendar time for an applicant who receives queries can therefore substantially exceed 30 days without any breach of the SLA.

FEES - the full schedule is now on the record at gazette strength, and the portal's live calculator page agrees with it line for line. The complete Schedule A/B/C was verified from TWO independent official renderings: the 9 April 2025 Jharkhand Gazette Extraordinary No. 165 (cited), and the Shramadhan portal's own 'Fee Structure of Factory Act' page (https://shramadhan.jharkhand.gov.in/factoryRegistrationRenewFeeStructure.action), which presents the identical matrix under the heading 'FEE BASED ON MAXIMUM NO OF PROPOSED EMPLOYEE & CAPACITY OF MACHINERIES (STRUCTURE VALID FROM 2025 ONWARDS)'. The two agree on every cell checked except one typographical divergence in the electricity schedule: for 'NOT EXCEEDING 6,00,000' KW transforming stations the gazette prints Rs 1,10,880 while the portal page prints Rs 84,000. The gazette figure should be preferred as the notified text. Note also that the gazette headnote titles these rules the 'Jharkhand Factories (Amendment) Rules, 2025', matching the ED record's attribution.

VALIDITY - the ED's validity text is confirmed but its rule citation is slightly off. The ED attributes the one-year minimum validity to 'The Jharkhand Factories (Amendment) Rules, 2025'. The notification that actually makes that change is the SEPARATE gazette of the same date (Jharkhand Gazette Extraordinary No. 164, 9 April 2025, notification dated 28 March 2025), which amends Sub rule (2) of Rule (5) and - despite being published in 2025 - is short-titled inside its own text 'the Jharkhand Factories (Amendment) Rules, 2023'. Its operative words confirm the ED's substance: 'Every license granted or renewed under this chapter shall remain valid or be in force for a minimum period of one year to maximum period of fifteen years as applicable. The licence so granted or renewed shall remain valid up to 31st December of the applied period.' The ED said 'a minimum license validity of one year, with longer-term options also offered' - correct, and the official maximum is now pinned at fifteen years. The fee/amendment gazette (No. 165) is the one properly short-titled 'Jharkhand Factories (Amendment) Rules, 2025'.

RISK-BASED INSPECTION - partially corroborated only, and not specific to the licensing site visit. The ED described a three-tier risk framework (low-risk exemption, medium-risk third-party certification, high-risk mandatory inspection) and flagged as MISSING the quantified thresholds separating the tiers. A Labour Department notification dated 02.12.2015 (Memo 2/F.A.-50-32/2015, read from the scanned Hindi original by page render) does establish the low-risk limb: low-risk industries with a satisfactory history of compliance with labour laws are granted exemption from the inspection process, or permitted self-certification in place of physical inspection under all labour laws, conditional on uploading the prescribed annual return to the Shramadhan portal by 30 June each year and maintaining the prescribed consolidated online register. It is framed as a general labour-law inspection reform, NOT as an exemption from the Factory Licence site visit, which the SOP still lists as mandatory Step 5. The quantified risk thresholds the ED flagged as MISSING remain unverified: CLASSIFICATION_OF_RISK.pdf was fetched successfully but is a scanned image with no text layer and was not read, so nothing is claimed from it.

UNREACHABLE THIS SESSION, so nothing is cited from them: advantage.jharkhand.gov.in (the Single Window portal named as the primary application route by the official SOP and by the CIF's own auto-renewal order) reset the connection on every https attempt and returned HTTP 503 'upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers' over http - this is a network/origin failure, not a TLS one, and the completed cert chain did not help. https://jharkhand.gov.in/labour also reset mid-session on re-fetch although https://jharkhand.gov.in/industries succeeded from the same host. Two files were fetched but yielded nothing readable and are cited for nothing: CLASSIFICATION_OF_RISK.pdf and Only%20Online%20Mandate.pdf (both scanned, no text layer). A web search surfaced Indian Kanoon reproductions of the Jharkhand Single Window Clearance Act 2015 Section 24 (deemed approval) - these were NOT treated as verification, as Indian Kanoon is not a government source and the snippets were never confirmed against an official gazette copy; nothing from them is cited or relied on above.
